rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes high-temperature tensile testing at 1000–1300 °C, whereas the paper used room-temperature compression, temperature-dependent indentation plastometry (RT–500 °C), and room-temperature scratch testing. These are different kinds of mechanical tests (tensile vs. compression/indentation/scratch) and different temperature regimes, so the intervention is a different kind of study.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies an inert argon atmosphere, 1000–1300 °C, and strain rates of ~10^-4 s^-1. The paper's conditions were room-temperature compression at 0.001 s^-1, indentation from RT to 500 °C in air, and scratch testing at RT. The temperature ranges and environments are entirely different, so there is no agreement on the paper's regime.

rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower yield strength but greater plastic strain and toughness for the HEA relative to tungsten at high temperature. The paper found higher strength (not lower) and greater plastic strain and toughness at its tested temperatures. The direction for plastic strain and toughness matches, but the yield strength prediction is opposite, and the temperature regime is different. This is the right property and direction in general terms only.
